rounds.proof_sketch: For size=128, block_size=256: Original num_blocks=(128+255)/256=383/256=1. Mutant num_blocks=(128+257)/256=385/256=1. Both evaluate to 1. Difference only occurs when size≥255 (e.g., size=255: original=1, mutant=2). Fixed shape [128,1] constrains size=128 permanently.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the ceiling division formula for num_blocks from (n+d-1)/d to (n+d+1)/d. With the fixed input shape [128,1], the flattened tensor always has exactly 128 elements. For this specific size with block_size=256, both arithmetic expressions evaluate to 1 through integer division (383/256=1 and 385/256=1). Since num_blocks depends solely on element count (not values), and the count is fixed by shape, no value variation can cause the mutant to compute a different num_blocks. The kernel launch, memory allocation, and all subsequent operations are identical between original and mutant.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The arithmetic mutation only produces different num_blocks when size reaches 255+ elements (where (size+255)/256 vs (size+257)/256 cross an integer boundary). With fixed size=128, both formulas yield num_blocks=1. Killing this mutant would require changing input shape to have ≥255 elements, which violates the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks for GPU kernels should treat launch parameter calculations specially. Mutations in grid/block dimension formulas often depend on input sizes, not values. Either (1) include shape variation in the test contract, or (2) identify such mutations as configuration-sensitive and flag them separately from value-testable mutations.
